beats.say: An explosion in space put the Apollo 13 crew in danger.
Launched from Kennedy Space Center on 11 April 1970, the mission was commanded by Jim Lovell, with Jack Swigert and Fred Haise.
Two days into the flight, an oxygen tank in the service module exploded and disabled the electrical and life support systems.
The crew quickly transferred to the Lunar Module as a lifeboat while Mission Control in Houston improvised new procedures to save them.
They successfully fixed the carbon dioxide scrubbers and returned safely to Earth on 17 April, as tens of millions watched. Would you have kept your cool during this mission?

facts: Apollo 13 took place from April 11 to April 17, 1970
The craft was launched from Kennedy Space Center on April 11, 1970
An oxygen tank in the service module exploded two days into the mission
The explosion disabled the electrical and life support system
The mission was commanded by Jim Lovell, with Jack Swigert as command module pilot and Fred Haise as Lunar Module pilot
The crew transferred to the Lunar Module as a lifeboat
Mission Control in Houston improvised new procedures to support the crew
The crew and mission controllers successfully improvised a solution for the carbon dioxide scrubber system
Tens of millions watched the splashdown on television
The crew returned safely to Earth on April 17
